title: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance: set how long policy matches are retained
summary: Hold: the table presents an automation command without documentation establishing that its parameter changes this setting. The permissions advice also overlooks restrictions on administrators scoped by administrative units, and today's preservation setting does not necessarily determine the period already stamped on older matches.

claims.claim: Neither the record nor the documentation confirms whether item 68688 is the existing Policy Match Preservation setting or a further change.

claims.claim: No rollout mechanics beyond the roadmap targets are stated for item 68688.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: A policy match stores a copy of the matching message rather than the original.
claims.quote: When a Communication Compliance policy finds a message that matches the policy, the solution stores a copy of the message (not the original message).

claims.claim: Learn says Policy Match Preservation can be used starting June 1, 2025.
claims.quote: Starting June 1, 2025, you can use the Policy Match Preservation setting to specify how long to save policy matches in Communication Compliance.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The documented preservation options are 1 month, 6 months, 1 year and 7 years.
claims.quote: You can choose 1 month, 6 months, 1 year, or 7 years.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The documented global Policy Match Preservation default is 1 year.
claims.quote: The default value is 1 year.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: A preservation period selected within a policy takes precedence over the global period.
claims.quote: The preservation period you select within a policy takes precedence over the global Policy Match Preservation setting.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The system automatically and permanently deletes policy matches older than the selected period.
claims.quote: The system automatically deletes policy matches that are older than the selected time period.
claims.fix: Keep the cited deletion behavior, but add: 'The channel-signals page still says copies are retained for as long as a policy is in place, which differs from the preservation-period behavior documented here.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/communication-compliance-channels, whose text says 'Communication Compliance policies retain copies of messages used for analysis and investigation for as long as a policy is in place'.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Preservation deletion affects the Communication Compliance copies, not the original messages in user shards.
claims.quote: Only the policy matches in Communication Compliance are deleted because they're copies of the original messages. This process doesn't delete original copies from user shards.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management can set retention policies for the original messages.
claims.quote: You can use Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management to set up a retention policy for original messages.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Changing the global time period applies going forward.
claims.quote: If you change the time period in the setting after September 1, the preservation period applies going forward.

claims.claim: Matches already stamped with an earlier global preservation period keep that earlier period.
claims.quote: if you select 1 year as the time period on September 1, then change the setting to 7 years on September 3, policy matches from September 1 and September 2 are preserved for 1 year, and policy matches starting on September 3 are preserved for 7 years.

claims.claim: What is configured today governs how long matches are kept.
claims.quote: if you select 1 year as the time period on September 1, then change the setting to 7 years on September 3, policy matches from September 1 and September 2 are preserved for 1 year
claims.fix: Replace 'what is configured today is what governs how long matches are kept' with 'changes to the global period apply going forward; earlier matches keep their previously stamped period', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/communication-compliance-investigate-remediate.
